exceptions.magnitude: -8.07 TWh, share -1.0pp (volume out of band) — C1 FAIL on keeper 2026-10-02-w0-pjm-fix2
exceptions.reason: OWNER RULING R-36, 2026-10-03 (owner card; recorded in docs/backcast-closeout-plan-2026-10.md §5.0 via PR #7107), verbatim: "Sign CT 2021 now; hold COAL_BIT 1b for NEXT-31". SIGNED MODEL-CLASS FRONTIER — documents the FAIL, does NOT reclassify it: rubric v3.1 makes C3c the only ledgerable criterion (calibration_verdict.LEDGERABLE_CRITERIA) and C1 is load-bearing, so the scorer ignores this entry fail-closed and the C1 FAIL stands; PJM stays NOT-YET. MECHANISM: PJM's out-of-merit commitment of CTs — the operator commits CTs in real time for local voltage, transfer and reserve needs that are unpublished and unit-specific, and pays them through balancing operating-reserve credits. An energy-only, cost-based LP commits only on its own economics. EVIDENCE: IMM 2021 SOM Table 4-3 (digitized at NEXT-26, results/phase0/pjm/_pjmnext26_bor_credits_by_zone_type.csv): CTs took 92.8 % of the $128 M of balancing generator credits (the 85.7 % cited in plan §3.6 is the 2023 value); real CTs ran ~2.5x the keeper's run blocks (6,547 vs 2,621) and put 8.4 TWh into out-of-money shoulder hours, 6.6 TWh more than the keeper (NEXT-24 §1-2); the under-run is across-plant and locational (AEP-Ohio, Dominion; Tait, Doswell, Louisa, Marsh Run among the top BOR recipients, NEXT-25/26) while within-plant loading matches real; NEXT-22/23 per-plant under-run at the dear CTs with the band already at the measured 1.05. WHY INEXPRESSIBLE: the commitment driver has no public forward-reproducible series (DA must-run-for-reliability is 0.3 % of DA MWh; the IMM dropped its zone tables after 2022); a floor built on observed CT output would be pinning (rule 13); plan §3.6 rules it ledger, inadmissible as a lever. EXHAUSTION RECORD (every CT lever adjudicated, PJM shard): ct_peaker_committed_measured U (across-plant object, min-run would not bind, worsens 2024/25; NEXT-22/23/24); netload_drag_floors K (CT -0.70 to -0.96 TWh at h13, not a closer); Tait 55248->2847 CAMPD remap is a rule-14 data repair riding the next solve (~$1-2/MWh), not a CT closer. RE-OPEN TRIGGER: a measured commitment-state input — unit-level BOR or RT-commitment records, or published local reliability requirements (the zonal DA pull would separate locational from conduct effects). A mechanism that lands there simply PASSes C1 and this entry goes inert. Source text: docs/records/pjm/DRAFT-closeout-pjm-2-frontier-text-2026-10-03.md Statement 2. Applied by closeout-PJM-impl (session_015xiQTucpy3uBh1rYQymzdS).

exceptions.reason: OWNER RULING R-37, 2026-10-03 (owner card; recorded in docs/backcast-closeout-plan-2026-10.md §5.0 via PR #7107), verbatim: "Documented FAIL; no re-open". DOCUMENTED FAIL, NOT ledgered and NOT an accepted limitation: rubric v3.1 makes C3c the only ledgerable criterion, so this entry is record only and the FAIL stands (PJM stays NOT-YET); no re-open of pjm_reserve_pergen_sync (stays R, census appended as evidence). ATTRIBUTION (docs/records/pjm/FINDING-closeout-pjm-2-2025-regression-attribution-2026-10-03.md): the whole PASS->FAIL move (incumbent pjmnext16_A_span -9.6 % / 0.182 -> W0 -11.6 % / 0.222) sits in 24 EMAAC VOLL hours (Jun 23-25, Jul 8/17/29-30): -1.205 of -0.993 $/MWh; 97 % of the crossing is the W0 fleet (seasonal_capacity_basis ~59 %, admit_standby_units ~41 % of +901 MW EMAAC in-zone capacity that EIA-860/923 show was real and ran in 2025) — both fields stay (rules 1, 14). The incumbent's PASS was the right level for the wrong reason: a single-zone $2,000 VOLL from a fleet missing ~900 MW, where the real event was system-wide heat-wave reserve scarcity (real system RT $470 mean over the 24 h, peak $1,830). FRONTIER CANDIDATE (docs/records/pjm/RESULT-closeout-pjm-2-heatwave-reserve-census-2026-10-03.md): the W0 reserve dual is 0 in every hour of 2025; in the 9 Jun 23-25 hours with real RT >= $400 the pool headroom is 6.5-8.2 GW against the 3.9 GW RTO requirement, 99.2 % of it on OFFLINE units (87.3 % offline CT/oil) that the not-online-gated pool counts as reserve; not an availability gap (the model already carries 5.6-7.7 GW more unavailable capacity than PJM's published outages, 0 of 9 hours with dU >= G). The open object is an online-gated reserve pool (whether offline quick-start capacity counts against PJM's synchronized/primary requirement in extreme-heat hours); prior verdicts pjm_reserve_pergen_sync R (pjm-h3), reserve_deliverability_scoping I, ordc_scarcity_overlay G (adder route closed). Applied by closeout-PJM-impl (session_015xiQTucpy3uBh1rYQymzdS).

entries.name: pjm_zonal_loss_surface (marginal delivery-factor surface)
entries.source: Ratio-of-sums dev_z,m = sum(MLC)/sum(MEC) per zone-month from PJM's published da_hrl_lmps type=ZONE record (all 21 transmission zones, DA basis; MEC published per row and identity-checked uniform across zones per UTC interval to 0.000000 $/MWh). Transmission zones roll up to model zones load-weighted by the metered hrl_load_metered series through the canonical eia930.zonal_shares._PJM_LOAD_ZONE_GROUPS crosswalk — every model zone is real, NONE interpolated. Frozen derive scripts/data/derive_pjm_loss_surface.py; offline acceptance 12/12 pair-years in [0.5x,1.5x] (ratios 0.95-1.07) before any solve. Charter: docs/records/pjm/FINDING-pjm136-zonal-dual-structure-2026-07-28.md.
entries.note: re-derive trigger is a source-data change only (rule 23), never a residual; representation bounds: one-way monthly linearization (reverse direction clamps to 0 — under-transmits in atypical-direction/congested hours), and the external star node carries NO loss (PJM_external is a fictitious pricing node with no published deviation), so seam-sourced energy is delivered lossless

entries.name: unit_outage_short_windows (< 5-day baseload-coal CEMS windows)

entries.source: per-unit EPA CAMPD hourly gross generation (scripts/data/derive_campd_unit_outages.py --short-windows); identification guards: coal-only detector + unit annual CF >= 0.55 (the partial-outage detector's baseload constant) + the revealed-availability in-merit filter (outage_detect.filter_revealed_outages; the full-stop override cannot engage below the 5-day cap)
entries.note: the >= 5-day duration floor makes event-coincident short forced outages invisible (MISO Jul 28-29 2025: ~2.8 GW coal offline at the peak block beyond the overlay; docs/records/miso/DIAGNOSIS-miso-july2025-lmp-2026-07.md); CT/CC event unavailability stays unmodeled pending a max-gen-event registry intake (no identification without it)
